Per-step cost is a pixel-proportional compute part plus a bandwidth-bound part (BN/GELU/pointwise, ~27% of a 32 px step, E043/E047) concentrated on large activations. Tip E036: 5.31 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Same-commit reruns read 0.7525 (E038), 0.7497 (E043) and 0.7544 (E047), so 3-seed noise is ±0.2 pp and the population mean is about 0.752, only ~0.2 pp over the 0.75 bar. Time noise is about ±0.04 s, with build-to-build drift (E043 5.29, E047 5.34, E036 5.31).

Mechanisms:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Pure step or epoch cuts (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045) trade at dial-like rates, so they are not free.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share (E028, E034, E036, E046), because frozen blocks skip memory-bound BN/GELU backward, optimizer updates and Lookahead traffic. E046 saved ~0.24 s at about −0.1 pp. The dose is nonlinear: E037's 60% freeze cost ~0.4 pp, while the late freezes were neutral.
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045) are null or negative. The recipe sits at a local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by −0.1 pp.
5. Systems-only math-identical work gives 1–2% each (E035). The E047 trace shows only ~2.5% of GPU time is outside the step graphs, so the ceiling for I076 is ~1–1.5%.
6. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded.
7. Sample dropping costs about as much as the dial.

structured_output.world_model:
W6 model after E047. Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost is a pixel-proportional compute part plus a bandwidth-bound part (BN/GELU/pointwise, ~27% of a 32 px step, E043/E047) concentrated on large activations. Tip E036: 5.31 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Same-commit reruns read 0.7525 (E038), 0.7497 (E043) and 0.7544 (E047), so 3-seed noise is ±0.2 pp and the population mean is about 0.752, only ~0.2 pp over the 0.75 bar. Time noise is about ±0.04 s, with build-to-build drift (E043 5.29, E047 5.34, E036 5.31).

Mechanisms:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Pure step or epoch cuts (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045) trade at dial-like rates, so they are not free.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share (E028, E034, E036, E046), because frozen blocks skip memory-bound BN/GELU backward, optimizer updates and Lookahead traffic. E046 saved ~0.24 s at about −0.1 pp. The dose is nonlinear: E037's 60% freeze cost ~0.4 pp, while the late freezes were neutral.
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045) are null or negative. The recipe sits at a local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by −0.1 pp.
5. Systems-only math-identical work gives 1–2% each (E035). The E047 trace shows only ~2.5% of GPU time is outside the step graphs, so the ceiling for I076 is ~1–1.5%.
6. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded.
7. Sample dropping costs about as much as the dial.

Misses: truncation savings were larger than my MAC-based models (E034, E037, E041, E046), accuracy swings of ±0.3 pp on identical code, and E037's cliff. Lesson: use wide accuracy ranges, treat 3-seed accuracy differences below 0.3 pp as noise, and expect bandwidth-bound levers to beat FLOP estimates.

Unsure: the true tip mean, selection bias of 0.1–0.2 pp, PCIe transfer of bandwidth-bound levers, whether the group-2 freeze can extend past 10%, and whether activation type matters for bytes moved.

Typical headroom: the tip's mean is barely above the bar, so any time-trading step must be paired with an accuracy source. A +0.25 epoch top-up buys ~0.1 pp for ~0.1 s.

forecasts.reason: E046 saved ~0.24 s and the +0.25 epoch adds ~0.1 s, so time is ~2–3% below E036. Accuracy is around the tip, with the top-up offsetting the freeze loss, but noise is large.
Math-identical systems work should save about 1–2% (~0.05–0.1 s), but the copies are partly cudagraph copy-in that is hard to remove. Accuracy moves only through rebuild noise.

ReLU saves a bool mask and cheaper elementwise work, so ~1–3% time. Accuracy likely drops about 0.1–0.3 pp because GELU suits this short-run recipe. The ≥3% time and ≤0.15 pp joint bar is unlikely to be met.

cruxes: Does the group-2 freeze keep its ~0.24 s saving and roughly neutral accuracy when measured against a same-build E036 on the same unselected seeds (13–32)?
How much of the E047 non-step GPU time (~135 ms, copies, interpolate, gathers) can be removed without a rebuild that shifts the kernel selection?
Is the true population mean of the tip above 0.752, so that the 0.75 bar leaves room for further time cuts?
